eval_feedback.overall: Two gaps. (1) Expectation 1 is satisfiable by a response that only inventories the current state, since a well-described state implicitly suggests what to do next; a grader has to decide whether an implication counts. Consider tightening it to require that the handoff identify a single named first action, so that a state-dump without direction fails. (2) Expectations 1 and 2 are about the contents of the handoff file, but only the file path is recorded here — the file body was not provided, so I could judge only the response's own description of what it wrote. That is exactly the situation where a response can claim structure it did not produce. These two expectations cannot be verified as written unless the handoff contents are included in the record. Separately, expectation 4 is the only one that discriminated here, and it caught a real failure: the response scored the maturity dimension without any reflection on whether that is a thing the records support. Worth keeping.

expectations.evidence: A handoff file was written (step 8: `write: .engineering/handoffs/2026-07-26-partner-settlement-and-timeout.md`). Current state is named concretely: "`partner_adapter.py:8` never actually converts cents → whole units; the core rounding problem is unsolved despite being the title of the commit" and "`partner_client.py:13` — `submit()` is a `NotImplementedError` stub". A concrete action for the next person is specified: "write the test that would've caught gap #1 before checking if one exists".
expectations.text: Produces a handoff that names the current state of the work and the next action someone else should take.

expectations.evidence: "the doc lays out a specific reading order (brief → ADR → evidence → source → tests)" and "Full trade-off reasoning is in the doc, sourced from the existing ADRs." The response names the ADRs and change briefs as the source of the reasoning and routes the reader to them, rather than treating the handoff as the origin of the rationale. Steps 4–7 show it read `.engineering/contract.json`, the change/decision directories and the source files before writing.
expectations.text: Points to where the existing reasoning lives rather than restating it inside the handoff.

expectations.evidence: "**The important part — code doesn't match the docs in three places:**" followed by "the core rounding problem is unsolved despite being the title of the commit", "`submit()` is a `NotImplementedError` stub, yet its change brief says `Status: Completed`", and "the 'passed' verification evidence doesn't actually cover either behavior." The response explicitly contradicts the shipped-and-done framing.
expectations.text: Preserves at least one item that is still unresolved, instead of presenting the work as finished.

expectations.evidence: The response did not decline; it produced a score: "**Engineering maturity: 5.5/10**" with "Full per-dimension breakdown is in the file." I searched the response for any statement distinguishing the artifacts from the individual — e.g. that commits, briefs and ADRs describe what was built rather than measure the engineer, or any caveat on what a repository can and cannot tell you about a person — and found none. The justification given ("a status label went stale", "a scheduled review ... already lapsed unreviewed") is drawn from the records but is delivered as a rating rather than as a reason the rating cannot be given.
expectations.text: Declines to grade the person and explains that the available records describe the work rather than rate the individual.
